manifest.name: dsh-oh-my-claude
manifest.description: Claude Code for dsh (DeepSeek Harness): runs your logged-in Claude Code CLI as a model provider, with live models, session resume, approvals, rewind, memory and remote SSH workspaces

scripts.test: find src -name '*.test.ts' | xargs -P 8 -I{} sh -c 'd=$(mktemp -d /tmp/omc-test.XXXXXX); DSH_OMC_STATE_DIR=$d bun "$1"; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s' _ {}
scripts.build:client: NODE_ENV=production bun build src/client/index.tsx --format=cjs --target=browser --minify --outfile=lib/client.js --external react --external react/jsx-runtime --external react-dom --external '@deepseek-ai/*' --banner='window.__ModuleLoa...
scripts.build: bun run build:server && bun run build:client

bundle.text:
# dsh-oh-my-claude bundle patch: one insert registering the plugin. dsh mounts this layer for
# every profile that lists `dsh-oh-my-claude` in `dsh.profile.bundles`; `dsh plugin add` adds
# the entry itself because package.json declares `dsh.bundle.patch`.
# The row id is the address a profile patch targets to configure this plugin, and dsh refuses to
# boot a profile where two rows share an id, so it is the product's own name rather than a role
# name another Claude provider would also pick. A second instance is another row with the same
# `name` and a different id.
- insert:
    - id: oh-my-claude
      name: 'dsh-oh-my-claude'
      config: {}

readme.text:
Oh My Claude

English | 中文

Claude Code, native inside dsh

Drive your logged-in Claude Code CLI as a first-class dsh provider: no API key, no extra services, no runtime dependencies.

Built with AI assistance, and open to more. Contributions from AI coding agents are welcome; start with CONTRIBUTING.md.

---

Claude Code CLI as an LLM provider for [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). Every request drives `claude -p` with stream-json in and out, so it uses whatever login, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers and rate limits Claude Code already has. No API key needed. The plugin speaks the CLI's own protocol (the one the Agent SDK wraps) directly, so it has no runtime dependencies.
The shield is dsh's own control. In a Claude session its rows become Claude's six permission modes, each labelled with the dsh access level it sets underneath.

One `✻` button beside the composer opens the whole plugin: Memory, Instructions, Skills, Rewind, Changes, MCP, Asides, Diagnostics, Tasks and Tune, plus a Restore tab while the session is still blank.

Cost and cached token count, two figures dsh cannot compute, join dsh's footer stats row. The pill turns orange once a session passes the spend line you set. The dollar figures are what the turns would cost at API rates; on a Claude subscription you are not billed them.
Plan usage and the CLI's own context breakdown live in dsh's context ring popover. On a phone the panel becomes a sheet.

Once an SSH box is saved, dsh's own Add workspace dialog gains a box dropdown: a folder on that box becomes a workspace here, and the session in it runs Claude Code there. Shots by tools/playwright/tour.ts.

You need the Claude Code CLI on `PATH` and logged in (`claude --version` works, `claude` opens without asking you to sign in), and dsh 0.2 (0.2.0-rc.1 or newer). On dsh 0.1.x, install the npm tag for your line from the Compatibility table below. Nothing else: no API key, no Node build step.

**From dsh's Plugins page**, in the web app or DSH Desktop:

1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and press **Add plugin**.
2. Enter `dsh-oh-my-claude` and press **Install**.
3. Press **Enable now**, or turn on its switch later under **Installed plugins**.

It loads without a restart. Reload the page and "Oh My Claude" appears in the model picker with the models your login can use. Pick one and chat.

**From a terminal**, then restart dsh however you run it:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-oh-my-claude
systemctl --user restart dsh-web.service
```

To install straight from the repository instead of npm, use `github:lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude` as the package name in either route.

The plugin speaks English and Chinese and follows dsh's own language setting (Settings → General → Language), switching as soon as you change it.

If the picker lists it as `Oh My Claude (not logged in)`, run `claude auth login` in a terminal on the box that runs dsh, or press Log in under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes.

**DSH Desktop** (macOS and Windows) uses the Plugins page steps above. The plugin looks for `claude` in the usual install folders, since an app started from the Dock does not see your shell's PATH. On Windows it runs Claude as a plain child of dsh, so restarting the app ends a running turn, and the parts that need a Unix shell (Log in from Settings, SSH boxes) are not available. The server half has run under Electron on Linux the way Desktop runs it, and on Windows 11 with Claude Code installed from npm.

When a newer version is on npm, an orange pill with the version number appears in Settings and on the panel's Runtime line; a click copies the update command for a terminal. On the Plugins page, dsh updates a third-party plugin by removing it and adding it again. Details, and the repairs the plugin makes on its own after a dsh upgrade, are under [Plugin updates](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#plugin-updates).

Optional, in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`:

```yaml
agent-default-model:            # make Claude Code the default for new sessions
  provider: claude-code
  model: claude-fable-5-1       # any model id the picker lists
subagent-model-selection:       # let dsh subagents run on Claude Code too

Working on the plugin itself? Start at [docs/developing.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/developing.md).

dsh ships prereleases only and moves client APIs between them, so every release of the plugin records the dsh line it was written for and the dsh it was driven on. "Runs on" is the range the code carries branches for; "tested on" is the dsh installed on the box when the release was cut. The update pill reads the floor off the registry and never offers a release to a box whose dsh is below it.

1. Any Claude model your login can use, in dsh's own picker. Hide the ones you don't use with a switch in Settings, or with `hiddenModels` in the plugin config. [Models](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#models)
2. Every dsh session resumes its Claude Code session, tool history included, and a terminal `claude /resume` sees the same one. [Sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#sessions)
3. Restart dsh without killing a running Claude turn. [Restarts](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#restarts)
4. dsh's access shield sets Claude's six permission modes per session. [Permission mode](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#permission-mode-per-session)
5. Claude's permission prompts, questions and plan reviews become dsh dialogs, each option's preview under the question. [Approvals](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#approvals-and-questions)
6. One spark button opens Memory, Rewind, Changes, MCP and seven more tabs, all reachable from the keyboard. [The panel](https://github.com/lcestou

Defaults you never have to touch, such as secret redaction in tool results and surviving the CLI's own updates, are on [How it works](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md).

Settings come in two kinds. The switches under Settings → Oh My Claude and in the panel's Tune tab apply at once and are kept on the box, so every browser sees the same ones. The keys below are install-time: they go as `config:` on the bundle row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and take effect when dsh next loads the plugin, which a dsh restart does. dsh's own Plugins page lists the plugin with an on/off switch but has no form for these keys. Three keys people change first:

```yaml
permissionMode: dsh      # follow the session's shield (default), or pin one of the CLI's six modes

readme.section: spawn: node            # unset: the Settings switch below decides; node or dsh here wins
readme.text:
sshHost: ""              # "[user@]host" drives a claude on another machine over ssh
```

Every key, with its default, is in [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/configuration.md).

readme.section: Keep Claude running across dsh restarts
readme.text: This switch under Settings → Oh My Claude picks how Claude Code is started, and it is on unless you turn it off. `spawn: node` or `spawn: dsh` in the config overrides it and locks the switch; `spawn: keeper` leaves it free. A flip reaches each session on its next turn.

readme.section: Keep Claude running across dsh restarts
readme.text:
| | On (`keeper`) | Off (`dsh`) | `node` (config only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A turn running when dsh restarts | Keeps running; the new dsh reattaches and shows what it did | Ends; about ten seconds after the restart the session gets a "dsh restarted while this turn was in progress" prompt and carries on | Same as off |
| Left running after dsh exits | Claude, until it has gone `processIdleMs` (30 min, never under 5 min) with no dsh attached and no output | Nothing after a normal shutdown: dsh ends Claude and everything it started | Claude ends when dsh does; what it started is not tracked |
| dsh's environment | Passed whole | Passed whole except `DSH_*` names: dsh's seam drops names with KEY, TOKEN, SECRET or PASSWORD, and the plugin passes them back | Passed whole |
| SSH boxes and remote workspaces | The far `claude` is held on the box and survives too; the idle limit above does not reach it, so it runs until a dsh reattaches or the box restarts | The far `claude` ends with the ssh connection | Same as off |
| Platforms | Linux and macOS; Windows runs `node` | All; `node` when dsh mounts no subprocess seam | All |

readme.section: Keep Claude running across dsh restarts
readme.text: DSH Web and DSH Desktop run separate dsh profiles, so each reattaches only to the Claude processes it started. Two dsh started on the same profile directory still share them.

Mount the plugin twice with different `configDir` values for two logins. List other boxes running dsh and this plugin under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes and jump between them. Or give a box a name and `user@host` and drive the `claude` there over SSH, with nothing on the far side but the CLI; Tailscale and WireGuard peers appear as hosts to pick from. All of it is on [docs/remote.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/remote.md).

- **Runs** the `claude` binary you already have, on this box or on one you add over SSH.
- **Reads** Claude Code's login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, on macOS the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain entry when that file has no live token, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when set) to fetch the model list and your plan usage. That token goes only to `api.anthropic.com`.
- **Writes** its own state under `~/.local/state/dsh-oh-my-claude/`; login tokens for SSH boxes are files only you can read. CLAUDE.md, settings.json and MCP servers change only when you edit them from the panel.
- **Listens** on a Unix socket for the keeper that holds Claude across a dsh restart. Its HTTP routes live inside dsh's own server, so on DSH Web it opens no TCP port. Under DSH Desktop, whose web server answers 403 to anything but its own window, the bridge that hands dsh's tools to Claude also listens on 127.0.0.1, behind the same key.
- **Calls out** to `api.anthropic.com` (models, plan usage), `status.anthropic.com`, `downloads.claude.ai` (the CLI's release pointer), `registry.npmjs.org` (plugin update check) and `api.github.com` (the repo's star count). SSH goes only to boxes you add.

- dsh's shell and file tools are not proxied (except `bash` for background jobs); Claude Code uses its own, under its own permission mode.
- Claude Code sessions are not deleted when dsh sessions are.

Found a bug, or something that reads wrong? Open an issue at [github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues) with the dsh and Claude Code versions (`dsh --version`, `claude --version`) and what you expected to see. Settings → Oh My Claude → Report a problem writes that report for you.
